newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent drifts at lower levels in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent drifts at lower levels in thin trade.

text.p: IPE Brent futures drifted at the lower levels they sank to in earlier trade at midday on Wednesday in thin trade, traders said.
August Brent was trading four cents lower at $17.83 a barrel at 1214 GMT, while July gas oil was 50 cents off at $159.75 a tonne.

Traders said most attention was focused on the outcome of OPEC talks which began in Vienna on Wednesday although few thought OPEC oil ministers would change the current nominal production ceiling of 25.03 million bpd.
News that OPEC members Saudi Arabia and Iran had convened a private session with quota buster Venezuela on Wednesday to "emphasise the need for quota compliance" had little impact on the market.
"It doesn't really mean much for the market unless something concrete comes of it," said one trader.

American Petroleum Institute (API) data had little impact on the market being mainly neutral in tone. The data showed that in the week ending June 20 crude oil stocks fell 756,000 barrels while gasoline stocks rose 592,000 barrels and middle distillates were up 905,000 barrels.

The resumption of Iraqi oil exports under the U.N. oil-for-food deal also loomed in the background. Iraqi oil minister Amir Rasheed told reporters in Madrid on Tuesday he expected them to resume in the next seven to ten days.

Under the first tranche of the deal running through the first six months of this year, Iraq sold $2 billion worth of crude oil. The second tranche will start once the aid distribution plan connected to the deal has been finalised. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
